title: Design patterns for implementing Hive Metastore for Amazon EMR on EKS
key_points: Three ways to run a standalone Hive Metastore for Spark on EMR on EKS: sidecar per job, one per cluster, or an external shared service, each deployed with the Spark Operator.
Only relevant to teams that cannot use the Glue Data Catalog; off the reader's path.
services: Amazon EMR on EKS, Apache Hive Metastore, Amazon EKS

title: Governing streaming data in Amazon DataZone with the Data Solutions Framework on AWS
key_points: Extends the DataZone catalog to Kafka topics: schemas from the Glue Schema Registry become catalog assets, and a custom approval flow grants subscribers IAM access to the MSK topic.
Deployed with CDK constructs from the open-source Data Solutions Framework; a Flink consumer shows the subscription in action.
Answers how to treat streams as governed data products; DataZone now sits inside SageMaker Unified Studio.
services: Amazon DataZone, Amazon MSK, AWS Glue Schema Registry, Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink, AWS CDK
decision: Ad hoc topic ACLs vs catalog-driven subscription and approval for access to streaming data
authors: Vincent Gromakowski, Francisco Morillo, Jan Michael Go Tan, Sofie Zilberman

title: Amazon Prime Video advances search for sports using Amazon OpenSearch Service
key_points: Prime Video added semantic (neural) search for live sports, using embeddings from a SageMaker-hosted model and no-ETL sync of catalog data from DynamoDB into OpenSearch.
Search-relevance story, off the reader's path.
services: Amazon OpenSearch Service, Amazon OpenSearch Ingestion, Amazon DynamoDB, Amazon SageMaker
authors: Amazon Prime Video — Radhika Chandak, Anna Chalupowicz, Yaliang Wu

Marketing note with no technical content.

title: Building and operating data pipelines at scale using CI/CD, Amazon MWAA and Apache Spark on Amazon EMR by Wipro
key_points: Wipro's framework lets engineers describe a Spark ETL job (sources, validation rules, SQL transforms, reconciliation) in JSON and a pipeline in YAML; Jenkins turns them into a jar and an Airflow DAG.
MWAA starts a transient EMR cluster, submits the jobs as concurrent steps, retries failures, alerts through SNS and terminates the cluster.
Each job runs in three phases with intermediate output kept in S3, so a rerun resumes from the last good phase.
services: Amazon EMR, Amazon MWAA, Apache Airflow, Apache Spark, Amazon SNS, Jenkins
decision: Licensed ETL tool vs config-driven Spark framework on transient EMR clusters orchestrated by Airflow

title: Supercharge your RAG applications with Amazon OpenSearch Service and Aryn DocParse
key_points: Partner walkthrough: Aryn DocParse and Sycamore split complex PDFs into labelled chunks, extract entities and tables, then load embeddings into OpenSearch for RAG with metadata filters.
Document-RAG preparation, off the reader's path.
services: Amazon OpenSearch Service, Aryn DocParse, Sycamore

title: Improve search results for AI using Amazon OpenSearch Service as a vector database with Amazon Bedrock
key_points: FAQ-style explainer on vector databases and why AWS positions OpenSearch as the vector store for Bedrock, including Bedrock knowledge bases on OpenSearch Serverless.
Marketing-level overview, off the reader's path.

title: Enhance your workload resilience with new Amazon EMR instance fleet features
key_points: EMR instance fleets gain prioritised instance-type fallback and smarter Availability Zone and subnet choice based on capacity, so clusters launch and scale when preferred types are scarce.
Cluster-capacity tuning for EMR on EC2 users.
authors: Deepmala Agarwal, Kashif Khan, Mandisa Nxumalo, Ravi Kumar Singh, Gaurav Sharma

title: Streamline AWS WAF log analysis with Apache Iceberg and Amazon Data Firehose
key_points: WAF logs stream through Firehose straight into an Iceberg table registered in the Glue Data Catalog and are queried with Athena, with no ETL job in between.
Gotcha: crawlers and Athena DDL lower-case column names, so the table is created through the Iceberg API in a Glue notebook to keep the logs' mixed-case fields matching.
Streaming writes leave many small files, so the post turns on catalog-managed compaction, snapshot expiry and orphan-file removal, or runs OPTIMIZE and VACUUM from Athena.
services: Amazon Data Firehose, Apache Iceberg, AWS Glue Data Catalog, Amazon Athena, AWS WAF
decision: Managed catalog compaction vs scheduled Athena OPTIMIZE for small files from streaming Iceberg writes
attaches_to: aws-bytes: File Layout Optimization (active, small-file compaction); real-time streaming (later)

title: Amazon Redshift announces history mode for zero-ETL integrations to simplify historical data tracking and analysis
key_points: Zero-ETL integrations into Redshift (Aurora PostgreSQL and MySQL, RDS for MySQL, DynamoDB) can keep every version of a source row instead of only the latest, adding active flag plus start and end timestamps.
Walkthrough replicates an Aurora PostgreSQL customer table and builds a type 2 slowly changing dimension from it with a scheduled stored procedure.
Kept versions grow the table, so plan sort keys on the history columns and periodic deletes plus vacuum of versions no longer needed.
services: zero-ETL (Aurora PostgreSQL to Redshift), Amazon Redshift, Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL, Amazon DynamoDB
decision: Zero-ETL history mode vs dbt snapshots vs DMS CDC with MERGE for keeping SCD2 history in the warehouse
attaches_to: aws-bytes: change data capture - DMS vs zero-ETL (later); dbt-pipelines (snapshots vs history mode)
authors: Raks Khare, Jyoti Aggarwal, Gopal Paliwal, Harman Nagra, Sumanth Punyamurthula

title: Migrate from Standard brokers to Express brokers in Amazon MSK using Amazon MSK Replicator
key_points: Moves an MSK Standard-broker cluster to a new Express-broker cluster by copying topics, data and consumer offsets with MSK Replicator, then cutting clients over all at once or in waves.
Superseded by the Nov 2026 in-place upgrade to Express brokers, which avoids building a second cluster.
services: Amazon MSK, Amazon MSK Replicator, Amazon MSK Connect

title: Foundational blocks of Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio: An admin’s guide to implement unified access to all your data, analytics, and AI
key_points: Admin view of SageMaker Unified Studio: domain setup, onboarding users and associated accounts, project profiles, blueprints and delegated domain units.
Platform-administration walkthrough, off the reader's path.
services: Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio, Amazon DataZone

title: Amazon Redshift Serverless adds higher base capacity of up to 1024 RPUs
key_points: AWS reports Serverless base capacity can now be set to 1024 RPUs, double the earlier ceiling, aimed at very large loads, memory-heavy queries and month-end peaks; max-capacity limits keep cost bounded.

AWS reports that on a 30 TB TPC-H test the larger base loaded data 44% faster for about 12% more cost, and ran the query suite 55% faster at about 11% lower total cost, mainly through far less spilling and S3 block fetching.
Lesson worth repeating: size with concurrent sessions, because AWS reports a 62% gain under concurrency but only 17% for a single sequential run.
decision: Smaller base RPU with auto-scaling vs larger base RPU vs price-performance target for heavy Serverless workloads
attaches_to: dbt-pipelines (Redshift Serverless sizing); aws-bytes: cost optimization (later)
authors: Ricardo Serafim, Harshida Patel, Milind Oke

title: Use DeepSeek with Amazon OpenSearch Service vector database and Amazon SageMaker
key_points: Hosts DeepSeek-R1 on a SageMaker endpoint and wires it into an OpenSearch RAG search pipeline through ML connectors, with Titan embeddings for the documents.
Search and model-hosting setup, off the reader's path.
services: Amazon OpenSearch Service, Amazon SageMaker, DeepSeek-R1

title: Handle errors in Apache Flink applications on AWS
key_points: Separates transient errors (timeouts, brief outages), which deserve retries, from permanent ones (bad payloads, logic bugs), which must not block the stream.
Flink patterns with code: Async I/O with a retry strategy for external calls, and side outputs that route failing records to a dead-letter sink while good records flow on.
Ends with what to do with dead-lettered records: inspect, fix and replay, or discard by policy; the ideas carry over to any stream consumer, including Kinesis and Lambda.
services: Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink, Apache Flink, Amazon Kinesis Data Streams
decision: Retry in place vs dead-letter sink vs side output for bad records in a streaming job
